newsitem.title: USA: Clinton would veto senate nuclear bill - White House.
newsitem.headline: Clinton would veto senate nuclear bill - White House.

text.p: President Clinton would veto a Senate nuclear waste bill as currently worded, the White House Office of Management and Budget said Monday.
"If S.104 were presented to the President in its current form, the President would veto the bill," OMB said in a "Statement of Administration Policy."

The bill would "undermine the credibility" of the U.S. nuclear waste disposal program because it would in effect designate a specified site for an interim storage facility before the appropriateness of that site as a permanent repository had been assessed, OMB said.
"The bill would also undermine the ongoing work on the permanent disposal site by siphoning away resources for an interim site," the statement said.
The Senate was expected Monday to take up a motion to proceed with the bill.

The Senate bill would effectively establish Nevada as the site of an interim nuclear waste storage facility before the viability assessment of Yucca Mountain, Nevada, as a permanent site was completed, OMB said.
